sections.h2: Where is Orange County, New York, and what does it include?
sections.html:
Orange County lies in the Hudson Valley, about 50 miles north of New York City in the southeast corner of the state, with Goshen as the county seat. It is the only New York county that touches both the Hudson and Delaware Rivers, and the only one that borders both New Jersey and Pennsylvania. The county has three cities, Middletown, Newburgh and Port Jervis, and it is split into 20 towns with a scattering of villages.

The land is varied. The Shawangunk Ridge marks the western edge, the Hudson Highlands run along the Rockland County line and south of Newburgh, and the Wallkill River valley fills the middle. In the south that valley opens into the Black Dirt Region, a former glacial lake bed known for farm soil. The county covers about 840 square miles and was created in 1683, then reorganized with its present boundaries in 1798.

Interstate 84, the Thruway (Interstate 87), Route 17 and the Palisades Parkway are the main roads. Stewart International Airport sits near Newburgh, and the Port Jervis Line of Metro-North serves the western end. Commuters to New Jersey and the city are a large part of the buyer pool.

sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Orange County?
sections.html:
Town, county and special district bills are mailed by the town and paid to the town collector without penalty during the collection window. Delinquent amounts and penalties go to the county Department of Finance, now on the third floor of the County Building at 255 Main Street in Goshen. The county's page lists 845-291-2480 for questions.

Three cities are carved out. The county does not collect or enforce taxes inside Middletown, Newburgh or Port Jervis, so owners there deal with the city directly. Properties outside those cities but inside the Middletown, Newburgh or Port Jervis school districts pay current school tax to the district and only pay the county once the bill turns delinquent.

  • County and town tax: collected January through March.
  • School tax: collected September through November.
  • Village tax: collected June through October, with an earlier start in a few villages.
  • Delinquent school tax from outside-city parcels reaches the county in March for Middletown, April for Newburgh and November for Port Jervis, according to this year's calendar.

sections.h2: How does the Orange County tax foreclosure auction work?
sections.html:
The county takes possession of parcels for unpaid tax through a foreclosure once a year, and the parcels are then offered at a public auction. A booklet with general information and the list of parcels is available from the Real Property Tax office before the sale. At this writing the county's auction page says no tax delinquency auctions are scheduled.

Parcels that do not sell go onto a leftover list that used to be open for bids each month, but the page says that deed sale process is paused because of recent changes to New York's Real Property Tax Law. Bids on the leftover list require official bank checks or money orders and a 10 percent deposit, not cash.

The county also posts surplus and non-surplus reports for the 2024 and 2025 auctions and the 2025 leftover list, which follow the state's Article 11 changes. The page tells anyone claiming surplus funds to consult an attorney. A seller who is behind should read that as a reason to settle the debt before foreclosure, since the owner's route to any leftover value now runs through a court filing.

sections.h2: What is the grievance and relief process in Orange County?
sections.html:
Assessments in Orange County are set by the town or city assessor, so complaints go to the local board of assessment review. State law opens those hearings on the fourth Tuesday of May unless a local law sets another date, and the State Tax Department advises checking the date with your assessor. If the board leaves the value unchanged, Small Claims Assessment Review is the lower-cost court route for most homeowners, and a tax certiorari case in State Supreme Court is the route that calls for an attorney.

The county's parcel search lets you look up owner, assessed values, tax maps, photos and comparable sales for any parcel, and it is useful before a grievance and before pricing a sale. For state relief, the STAR credit is registered through the State Tax Department's Homeowner Benefit Portal, and a seller should close that registration at the sale.

sections.h2: How do I sell an Orange County house that has tax due?
sections.html:
Work out which collector holds the balance. In a town, current bills sit with the town collector until the window closes and then move to the county Department of Finance. In Middletown, Newburgh or Port Jervis, call the city.

  1. Ask for a payoff figure in writing, with the date it is good through.
  2. Ask whether foreclosure has started on the parcel.
  3. Give the figure to your attorney so it is paid at closing.
  4. Close your STAR registration if you receive that benefit.

A buyer paying cash can purchase the house as it is, with the lien, any repairs and any tenants. That helps when the clock is short, because a financed buyer's appraisal and lender timeline may not fit before the county acts.

faqs.q: Where do I pay delinquent property tax in Orange County, NY?
faqs.a: Delinquent county and town tax goes to the Orange County Department of Finance, on the third floor of the County Building at 255 Main Street in Goshen. The number on the county's pages is 845-291-2480. Inside the cities of Middletown, Newburgh and Port Jervis the county does not collect, so call the city.

faqs.q: When are Orange County property tax bills collected?
faqs.a: Collection periods vary by town, but county and town tax is generally collected January through March, school tax September through November and village tax June through October. Your own bill states the dates that apply, and your municipality's collector can confirm them.

faqs.q: Is the Orange County tax auction happening now?
faqs.a: The county's auction page currently states that no tax delinquency auctions are scheduled. It also says the leftover list deed sale is paused because of changes to state tax law. Sign up for the page's email alerts or ask the Real Property Tax office for updates.

faqs.q: What can I do if I think my Orange County assessment is too high?
faqs.a: File a complaint with your town or city board of assessment review, which meets starting the fourth Tuesday in May unless a local law sets another date. If that fails, Small Claims Assessment Review is open to most homeowners. Call your assessor first, since an informal talk can fix errors.

faqs.q: Can I sell my house in Orange County before foreclosure?
faqs.a: Yes. The county can only auction a parcel once foreclosure is complete, and a sale that pays the full tax lien at closing clears the debt. Ask Finance for a written payoff and which stage your parcel has reached, and do not wait for an auction notice.
